conversations.title: Late Arrival at ALMOND
conversations.summary: A young woman arrives late to meet her friend outside ALMOND in Roppongi and they decide on somewhere to eat.
conversations.note: 今来たとこ is a casual shortening of 今来たところ, meaning 'I just got here'. Ramen and udon are popular cheap options around Roppongi, and Roppongi Crossing is busy enough that people often agree on a landmark like ALMOND to meet.

speakers.name: つむぎ
speakers.about: Young woman in her early 20s, bright and casual, a bit flustered about being late

speakers.name: 武宏
speakers.about: Young man in his 20s, friendly and easygoing, her close friend

lines.ja: ごめーん、ちょっと遅れた！待った？
lines.en: Sorry, I'm a bit late! Have you been waiting?

lines.ja: ううん、今来たとこ。六本木駅、混んでた？
lines.en: No, I just got here. Was Roppongi Station crowded?

lines.ja: 4a出口から出たら、道わかんなくなっちゃって。
lines.en: When I came out of Exit 4a, I totally got lost.

lines.ja: ここ交差点だからね。アマンドの前でよかったよ。
lines.en: It's a big intersection, so it's easy to get lost. Good thing we met in front of ALMOND.

lines.ja: ほんとごめん。おなか空いたよね。何食べる？
lines.en: I'm really sorry. You must be hungry. What should we eat?

lines.ja: 寒いし、あったかいラーメンはどう？一風堂とか。
lines.en: It's cold, so how about some warm ramen? Ippudo, maybe.

lines.ja: えー、一風堂めっちゃ並んでそう。みのち庵のうどんは？
lines.en: Ugh, Ippudo's probably got a huge line. How about udon at Minochi-an?

lines.ja: いいね。あそこ、夜は静かだし。じゃあ行こっか。
lines.en: Sounds good. It's quiet there at night. Shall we go?

lines.ja: うん！ちょっと歩くけど、大丈夫？
lines.en: Yeah! It's a bit of a walk, but is that okay?

lines.ja: 大丈夫、大丈夫。行こう。
lines.en: Totally fine. Let's go.

conversations.title: Lunch Decision at Roppongi Crossing
conversations.summary: Two coworkers on their lunch break weigh AFURI ramen against Thai gapao, worried about the queue and the afternoon meeting.
conversations.note: The verb 並ぶ (narabu) means to line up or queue, and 〜てる is the casual form of 〜ている, as in 並んでるよね. Japanese speakers often soften guesses with 〜かな or 〜かも, as in 十分くらいかな and すぐ入れるかも.

speakers.name: 田中さん
speakers.about: Man in his late 20s, office coworker, friendly and easygoing

speakers.name: ユイ
speakers.about: Woman in her 20s, office coworker, calm and practical

lines.ja: ユイさん、お昼どうする？
lines.en: Yui, what do you want for lunch?

lines.ja: うーん、AFURIのラーメンにする？
lines.en: Hmm, should we go for AFURI ramen?

lines.ja: いいね。でも、いつも並んでるよね。
lines.en: Sounds good. But there's always a line, right?

lines.ja: うん、駅の前だしね。十分くらいかな。
lines.en: Yeah, it's right by the station. Maybe ten minutes?

lines.ja: 十分ならいいけど、午後の会議があるからなあ。
lines.en: Ten minutes is fine, but we have a meeting this afternoon.

lines.ja: じゃあ、タイ・ガパオ東京はどう？すぐ入れるかも。
lines.en: Then how about Thai Gapao Tokyo? We might get in right away.

lines.ja: ガパオか、いいね。ランチセットも安いし。
lines.en: Gapao, nice. The lunch set is cheap too.

lines.ja: でしょ？ついでにデイリーヤマザキで飲み物も買おうよ。
lines.en: Right? Let's grab drinks at Daily Yamazaki on the way.

lines.ja: 了解。六本木交差点を渡ったら、すぐそこだね。
lines.en: Got it. Once we cross Roppongi Crossing, it's right there.

lines.ja: うん、信号が青になるまで待とう。
lines.en: Yeah, let's wait until the light turns green.

conversations.title: Forgotten Umbrella at Roppongi Crossing
conversations.summary: It starts raining outside ALMOND at Roppongi Crossing, and one friend forgot an umbrella, so the other suggests buying a cheap one nearby.
conversations.note: ビニ傘 (vinyl umbrella) is the cheap plastic umbrella sold at every konbini in Tokyo, and buying one on a rainy day is a common habit. The casual contractions じゃん and ちゃう are typical of friends talking.

speakers.name: ユイ
speakers.about: early 20s, bright and casual, a university student

speakers.name: 健太
speakers.about: mid 20s, friendly and easygoing, ユイ's friend

lines.ja: あーもう、雨じゃん。傘持ってくるの忘れた。
lines.en: Ugh, it's raining. I forgot to bring an umbrella.

lines.ja: マジで？今朝は晴れてたのにね。
lines.en: Seriously? It was sunny this morning.

lines.ja: 最悪…ずぶ濡れになっちゃうよ。
lines.en: The worst... I'm going to get totally soaked.

lines.ja: 六本木駅4a出口の近くのデイリーヤマザキで、ビニ傘売ってるよ。
lines.en: The Daily Yamazaki near Roppongi Station Exit 4a sells vinyl umbrellas.

lines.ja: え、本当？じゃあ、ちょっと買ってくる。
lines.en: Really? Then I'll go buy one real quick.

lines.ja: 一本で足りる？二人で入れる大きいやつ、買ったほうがいいかも。
lines.en: Will one be enough? You might want a big one we can both fit under.

lines.ja: 確かに。じゃあ、大きめのにしようかな。
lines.en: You're right. Then I think I'll get a bigger one.

lines.ja: いいね。買ったら、アマンドの前で待ってるね。
lines.en: Sounds good. I'll wait for you in front of ALMOND once you've got it.

conversations.title: Last Train or Karaoke
conversations.summary: Two friends outside ALMOND in Roppongi argue about catching the last train home or staying out at karaoke until the first train.
conversations.note: 終電 is the last train and 始発 is the first train, so 始発まで means until morning. The casual phrase ちょっとだけ (just a little) is often used to talk a friend into something, and the other person's reply is a playful way of calling it out.

speakers.name: ユイ
speakers.about: early 20s woman, bright and casual, pushing for karaoke

speakers.name: ケンタ
speakers.about: early 20s man, friendly but sensible, has a shift tomorrow

lines.ja: ねえ、もう終電じゃない？
lines.en: Hey, isn't it the last train time already?

lines.ja: まだ大丈夫だって。六本木駅、すぐそこじゃん。
lines.en: It's fine. Roppongi Station is right there.

lines.ja: 終電、十二時過ぎじゃなかった？
lines.en: Wasn't the last train after midnight?

lines.ja: 終電まだあるよ。4a出口から行けば間に合う。
lines.en: There's still one. If we go from Exit 4a, we'll make it.

lines.ja: でもさ、せっかくだからカラオケ行かない？始発まで。
lines.en: But hey, since we're already out, how about karaoke until the first train?

lines.ja: えー、朝まで歌うの？明日、朝からバイトなんだけど。
lines.en: Seriously, singing till morning? I have a morning shift tomorrow.

lines.ja: 大丈夫、ちょっとだけだって。ファミマで飲み物買えばいいじゃん。
lines.en: Don't worry, just a little. We can grab drinks at FamilyMart.

lines.ja: ちょっとだけ、が一番あぶないんだよ。前もそう言ってたじゃん。
lines.en: "Just a little" is the most dangerous thing. You said that last time too.

lines.ja: 今日は本当に歌うだけ。ね、お願い！
lines.en: Tonight it's really just singing. Please, come on!

lines.ja: しょうがないなあ。じゃあ、一時間だけね。
lines.en: Fine. But only one hour.

lines.ja: やった！じゃあ、交差点の向こうのカラオケにしよう。
lines.en: Yes! Then let's go to the karaoke across the intersection.

lines.ja: 了解。終電は…もう諦めるか。
lines.en: Got it. The last train... guess I'll give up on it.

conversations.title: Weekend Chat at Roppongi Crossing
conversations.summary: Two coworkers bump into each other near ALMOND on the way to the office and catch up on their weekends.
conversations.note: Casual speech drops the polite ending, as in 行こう, 見てきた, and じゃん, while the more polite speaker keeps ですか and ですけど. The phrase ちょうどよかった is a common way to say "Perfect timing" when you run into someone.

speakers.name: ユイ
speakers.about: Woman in her 20s, a junior coworker, friendly and a bit tired on a Monday

speakers.name: 佐藤さん
speakers.about: Man in his late 20s, a senior colleague, easygoing and warm

lines.ja: 佐藤さん、おはようございます！
lines.en: Good morning, Mr. Sato!

lines.ja: あ、ユイさん。おはよう。ちょうどよかった、一緒に行こう。
lines.en: Oh, Yui. Morning. Perfect timing, let's go together.

lines.ja: 六本木駅から出たら会えるなんて。週末どうでした？
lines.en: I didn't expect to run into you right after coming out of the station. How was your weekend?

lines.ja: 楽しかったよ。土曜日、ミッドタウンで展覧会見てきた。
lines.en: It was fun. On Saturday I went to see an exhibition at Tokyo Midtown.

lines.ja: いいですね！どの展覧会ですか？
lines.en: Nice! Which exhibition was it?

lines.ja: 写真の展覧会。すごく静かで、落ち着いたよ。
lines.en: A photography show. It was really quiet and calming.

lines.ja: 私は日曜、ずっと家で寝てました。ちょっと疲れちゃって。
lines.en: I spent all of Sunday sleeping at home. I was kind of worn out.

lines.ja: それもいい休みじゃん。
lines.en: That's a pretty good rest too, right?

lines.ja: まあ、そうですけど。あ、見て。アマンドの前、人多いですね。
lines.en: I guess so. Oh, look. There are a lot of people in front of Almond.

lines.ja: 今日は暑くなるみたいだね。早く行こうか。
lines.en: Looks like it'll get hot today. Shall we hurry on?

conversations.title: Asking the Way to Midtown
conversations.summary: A visitor from Osaka politely asks a local office worker how to walk to Tokyo Midtown from the Roppongi Crossing.
conversations.note: すみません、ちょっとお聞きしてもいいですか is the standard polite opener when approaching a stranger. Directions often use ～ば forms like 行けばいい and sentence endings like ～ですよ to sound friendly and considerate.

speakers.name: 中村さん
speakers.about: man in his 20s visiting from Osaka, polite and a little nervous

speakers.name: 佐々木さん
speakers.about: woman in her 30s, office worker, kind and composed

lines.ja: すみません、ちょっとお聞きしてもいいですか。
lines.en: Excuse me, may I ask you something for a moment?

lines.ja: はい、何でしょうか。
lines.en: Yes, what can I do for you?

lines.ja: 東京ミッドタウンに行きたいんですけど、どう行けばいいですか。
lines.en: I'd like to go to Tokyo Midtown. How should I get there?

lines.ja: ミッドタウンですね。ここから歩いて十分くらいですよ。
lines.en: Midtown, is it? It's about a ten-minute walk from here.

lines.ja: えっ、そんなに近いんですか。大阪から来たので、迷いそうで。
lines.en: Oh, it's that close? I came from Osaka, so I think I might get lost.

lines.ja: 外苑東通りをまっすぐ北へ行くだけです。右手に見えてきますよ。
lines.en: Just go straight north along Gaien-Higashi-dori. You'll see it on your right.

lines.ja: 外苑東通りを北ですね。途中で信号は多いですか。
lines.en: North on Gaien-Higashi-dori, got it. Are there many traffic lights on the way?

lines.ja: いいえ、大きい交差点は一つだけですよ。
lines.en: No, there's only one big intersection.

lines.ja: 分かりました。ありがとうございます、助かりました。
lines.en: Got it. Thank you so much, you've been a great help.

lines.ja: いえいえ。楽しんできてくださいね。
lines.en: Not at all. Enjoy your visit!

conversations.title: Waiting for a Late Friend
conversations.summary: Two students outside ALMOND wait for a friend who is running late and decide to move to a café nearby.
conversations.note: Casual reported speech uses ～って (e.g. 電車が混んでるって, meaning "he said the train is packed"), which you'll hear constantly in friends' talk. ～じゃない？ is a soft way to check a guess, like "isn't it...?"

speakers.name: 春日部つむぎ
speakers.about: university student, early 20s, bright and chatty

speakers.name: 玄野武宏
speakers.about: university student, early 20s, easygoing and practical

lines.ja: ケンタ、まだ来ないね。
lines.en: Kenta still hasn't shown up, huh.

lines.ja: もう二十分くらい遅れてない？
lines.en: Isn't he already like twenty minutes late?

lines.ja: 電車が混んでるって連絡来た。
lines.en: He messaged saying the train is packed.

lines.ja: じゃあ、ここに立って待つのもしんどいね。
lines.en: Then standing here waiting is going to be tiring.

lines.ja: 中で待つ？ルノアールでいい？
lines.en: Want to wait inside? Is Renoir okay?

lines.ja: ルノアール混んでそうじゃない？タリーズ行こうよ。
lines.en: Renoir looks crowded, doesn't it? Let's go to Tully's.

lines.ja: いいよ。六本木駅の4a出口の近くだよね。
lines.en: Sure. It's near Exit 4a of Roppongi Station, right?

lines.ja: そう。ついでにファミマで飲み物買っていい？
lines.en: Yeah. Can I grab a drink at FamilyMart on the way?

lines.ja: いいけど、コーヒー代はケンタのおごりね！
lines.en: Sure, but Kenta's paying for the coffee!

lines.ja: それは確かに。
lines.en: Fair enough.

conversations.title: Mom and Daughter at Roppongi Crossing
conversations.summary: A mother visiting from the countryside and her Tokyo daughter stand outside ALMOND and plan a drugstore stop for pollen-season supplies.
conversations.note: ついでに means picking up something while you are already out, and ドラッグストア is the usual word for a drugstore in Japan, where you can buy medicine, tissues and eye drops. Locals often call the same place 薬局 when they mean a pharmacy counter, so the two words overlap a bit.

speakers.name: お母さん
speakers.about: Mother, 50s, visiting from the countryside, warm and polite

speakers.name: ユイ
speakers.about: Daughter, 20s, lives in Tokyo, relaxed and practical

lines.ja: 六本木って、本当に人が多いね。
lines.en: Roppongi really has a lot of people, doesn't it?

lines.ja: うん、いつもこんな感じだよ。ここアマンドの前、待ち合わせの定番なんだ。
lines.en: Yeah, it's always like this. This spot in front of ALMOND is the classic meeting place.

lines.ja: へえ、ここが有名なアマンドなのね。
lines.en: Oh, so this is the famous ALMOND.

lines.ja: ねえ、花粉もうひどい？
lines.en: So, is the pollen bad already?

lines.ja: そうなのよ。目がかゆくて、もう困ってるの。
lines.en: It really is. My eyes are itchy and I'm already having trouble.

lines.ja: じゃあ、駅の近くのドラッグストアで何か買おうか。
lines.en: Then let's pick something up at the drugstore near the station.

lines.ja: 目薬も欲しいし、マスクもまだ残ってるかしら。
lines.en: I want eye drops too, and I wonder if there are still masks left.

lines.ja: マスクならたくさんあるよ。目薬はこっちの棚だね。
lines.en: There are plenty of masks. The eye drops are on this shelf.

lines.ja: あら、いろいろあって迷っちゃうわ。
lines.en: Oh my, there are so many kinds, I can't decide.

lines.ja: いつものでいいじゃん。ついでにのど飴も買っとこう。
lines.en: Just get your usual. Let's grab some throat drops while we're at it.

conversations.title: Late Dinner Plans at the Crossing
conversations.summary: Two tired office workers leaving late outside ALMOND decide on a quick, warm soba dinner nearby and chat about the chilly night.
conversations.note: Casual forms like 遅くなっちゃった (from 〜ちゃう) and 〜じゃん show friendly speech between colleagues, while 立ち食いそば is a cheap, quick standing soba shop. Note that 〜しよう is a natural way to suggest a decision together.

speakers.name: 田中さん
speakers.about: man in his 30s, office worker, tired but easygoing

speakers.name: ユイ
speakers.about: woman in her late 20s, coworker, practical and composed

lines.ja: 今日も遅くなっちゃったね。お腹すいた。
lines.en: We got held up again today. I'm starving.

lines.ja: ほんとだね。もう九時過ぎだよ。
lines.en: Seriously. It's already past nine.

lines.ja: 軽く何か食べて帰ろうか。立ち食いそばとかどう？
lines.en: Shall we grab something quick before heading home? How about standing soba?

lines.ja: いいね。でも今夜は冷えるね。
lines.en: Sounds good. But it's really cold tonight, isn't it?

lines.ja: 本当だ。風が強くて、ちょっと寒いね。
lines.en: It really is. The wind's strong and it's a bit chilly.

lines.ja: 温かいそばなら、ちょうどいいかも。
lines.en: A hot bowl of soba would be perfect, then.

lines.ja: 駅の近くのみのち庵、まだ開いてるはず。
lines.en: Minochi-an near the station should still be open.

lines.ja: じゃあそこにしよう。安いし、すぐ食べられるし。
lines.en: Then let's go there. It's cheap and we can eat right away.

lines.ja: 了解。交差点を渡ってすぐだよ。
lines.en: Got it. It's right across the crossing.

lines.ja: 雨が降る前に行こうか。
lines.en: Let's go before it starts raining.

conversations.title: Friday Night Plans at Roppongi Crossing
conversations.summary: Two friends outside ALMOND at Roppongi Crossing argue lightly about takoyaki, the walk to Tokyo Midtown, and how much beer they will drink.
conversations.note: じゃん is a casual sentence ending that softens a point, like 'you know' or 'right'. 一杯だけ ('just one drink') is a classic line people tease friends about, and 銀だこ is a takoyaki chain with a shop near Roppongi Station.

speakers.name: ミサキ
speakers.about: early 20s, bright and chatty, likes teasing her friend

speakers.name: ダイキ
speakers.about: early 20s, easygoing and friendly, a bit lazy about walking

lines.ja: 金曜の夜って、やっぱ混んでるね。
lines.en: Friday nights are always so crowded, huh.

lines.ja: 本当だね。とりあえず、どこ行く？
lines.en: For real. So, where should we go first?

lines.ja: まず、銀だこ買って歩きながら食べない？
lines.en: How about we grab some Gindako and eat while we walk?

lines.ja: えー、また銀だこ？ この前も食べたじゃん。
lines.en: Ugh, Gindako again? We just had it last time.

lines.ja: だって美味しいじゃん。ミッドタウンまで歩こうよ。
lines.en: But it's good! Let's walk over to Midtown.

lines.ja: 歩くのやだよ。ヒルズの方が近くない？
lines.en: I don't want to walk. Isn't Hills closer?

lines.ja: ダイキ、最近運動不足って言ってたじゃん。
lines.en: Daiki, you said you've been short on exercise lately.

lines.ja: それは言ったけどさ。ミサキこそ、遅刻三回したくせに。
lines.en: I said that, sure. But you were late three times, remember?

lines.ja: それは電車が遅れたの！ 今日は時間どおりに来たし。
lines.en: That was the train being late! I got here on time today.

lines.ja: まあね。じゃあ、そのあと居酒屋ね。ビールは一杯だけ。
lines.en: Fair enough. Then izakaya after that, and just one beer.

lines.ja: 一杯だけって、いつもそう言うじゃん（笑）。
lines.en: You always say 'just one', though (lol).

lines.ja: 今日は本当に一杯だけ。ほら、行こう。
lines.en: Today it really is just one. Come on, let's go.
